prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent PNG replacement sprite atlas for a painted fantasy board-game map.
Create exactly SIX isolated miniatures in THREE equal columns and TWO equal rows, row-major order. Canvas1536x1024. Each object fits within65percent of its512x512cell with wide fully transparent gutters. GENUINE TRANSPARENT ALPHA, no background color, no paper, checkerboard, text, labels, grid, land islands or blue water pads. Only narrow broken translucent grey-blue ripples immediately at hull/water contacts.
Style: fine European storybook gouache, gently elevated three-quarter overhead view, softly lit upper-left, muted grey-brown aged timber, faded flax/ivory sails, soft slate-blue dolphins. Match subdued detailed fantasy board-map structures. No shiny3D, toy models, cartoon outlines, modern engines, flags, cannons, pirates or neon. All vessels must read as BIG full-size ships with long enclosed hulls and numerous small details. NOT small rowboats blown up: no dinghies, huge oars, open canoe hulls, giant single crates, or cockpit filling whole boat. Cabin doors, railings, hatches, ropes, cargo must be tiny relative to the ship; no visible humans needed.
Exact subjects:
1. A substantial late-medieval merchant cog: high sterncastle with small cabin windows, deep broad plank hull, two masts with several weathered square sails, visible deck hatches and fine railings. Wide three-quarter view showing whole long hull.
2. A large working fishing vessel: decked oak hull, raised small wheelhouse at stern, two modest masts and furled canvas, tiny net racks, small stacked barrels and working deck. Full-size offshore fishing boat, never a tiny skiff.
3. A handsome two-masted merchant schooner: long hull, several layered pale linen sails, bowsprit, tiny aft cabin, visible deck railing, no flags. Clearly a substantial sailing ship.
4. A broad flat-bottomed cargo barge: long plank hull, a small roofed deckhouse at the stern, numerous tiny bundled timber stacks and covered cargo bales along its broad deck. A substantial river transport, not a log raft.
5. A partially sunk large merchant shipwreck: long broken hull with miniature cabin ruins and two snapped masts, tilted spars and faint waves at waterline; structure clearly from a large ship, not wrecked dinghy.
6. A close pair of dolphins leaping side by side, two distinct gracefully arcing bodies at slightly different heights, tiny splashes; muted slate-grey painted natural anatomy. Compact pair, not a single giant dolphin.
Strict3columns x2rows. Six separate models, centered one per cell, actual transparency with no opaque water bases. Maintain restrained colors and clear silhouettes.
